ai_summary: Scotland's electricity network currently highlights a striking regional disparity in generation and carbon performance, with Scottish carbon intensity standing at an ultra-clean 1 gCO2/kWh compared to 165 gCO2/kWh GB-wide. Across Great Britain, GB wind output is delivering 3.4 GW, with estimated Scottish wind output contributing 1.5 GW, representing 14.9% of installed Scottish wind capacity. Despite this abundant renewable supply, internal transmission bottlenecks restrict full export to southern demand centres. Consequently, 490 MWh of Scottish generation has been curtailed so far today through the Balancing Mechanism, incurring a constraint cost of about £30,168. To replace this blocked green energy, fossil generation was ramped up down south, with an estimated 93,100 m3 of gas burned elsewhere, needlessly adding 172 tonnes of CO2 to the atmosphere. Extrapolating today’s constraint figures indicates an estimated total yearly cost of curtailment of approximately £11 million. When socialised across total national electricity demand, this adds an estimated £0.04/MWh to everybody's invoice in the UK, reinforcing the urgent operational need for accelerated transmission infrastructure reinforcement to capture low-cost, zero-carbon Scottish power.
